title: PROTECT separates beta-cell preservation from clinical outcomes
population: 328 children and adolescents ages 8–17 with recently diagnosed type 1 diabetes, randomized 217 versus 111.
outcome: Stimulated C-peptide change at week 78; key secondary outcomes include insulin dose, HbA1c, time in range and clinically important hypoglycemia.
finding: The authors report a higher stimulated C-peptide level at week 78 in the teplizumab group versus placebo, with a between-group difference of 0.13 pmol/mL (95% CI 0.09–0.17). The original key secondary endpoints did not differ significantly.
limitations: C-peptide measures insulin production and does not establish insulin independence or clinical benefit. The accelerated approval indication is not evidence of a cure. The sample is source-checked, not independently expert-reviewed.
